newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine Senate passes bill to sell mortgage bank.
newsitem.headline: Argentine Senate passes bill to sell mortgage bank.

text.p: The Argentine Senate passed late Thursday a bill to privatize the state mortgage lender Banco Hipotecario which has been valued at $2.5-$3.0 billion.
The bill was passed by the lower chamber in May and was approved by the Senate minutes before midnight. The ruling Peronist Party commands a majority in both chambers.
President Carlos Menem has vowed proceeds from Hipotecario's sale will be channelled to public works, mainly house building, and create jobs in a country ridden with a 17.3 percent unemployment rate.
According to private news agency DyN $100 million are earmarked to finance house building in the poorer provinces and another $100 million would go to capitalize state-run Banco Nacion.
The remainder would be split in halves between the central government and the provinces.

The bill creates a trusteeship managed by Banco Nacion and controlled by a Congressional committee to administrate the sale proceeds and advise both the central goverment and the provinces in their infrastructure building plans.
Hipotecario has the largest assets of any Argentine bank, at $4.31 billion, and last year made a profit of $306 million, versus $327 million a year earlier.
Plans to sell it were launched last September and sparked criticism both from the Peronist Party and the opposition.
Critics fear Hipotecario's privatization could end the bank's role in providing home loans under soft conditions.
